evidence: corpus.py:125 `proc.wait()` return value is discarded — no returncode check
corpus.py:116-123 a shortfall in stdout lines simply leaves entries out of `contents`
corpus.py:140-146 `raw = bodies.get(b.sha)` / `if raw is None: continue` — a missing blob is silently skipped
By contrast `_git_stdout` (corpus.py:59-65) uses `check=True`; the bulk path has no equivalent liveness assertion
ABSENCE: no assertion that the number of successfully-read blobs equals len(content_shas), so 'read every blob' cannot be distinguished from 'git died mid-stream'
advisory.finding: _batch_cat launches `git cat-file --batch` via Popen and never inspects proc.wait()'s return code; a git failure or partial/truncated output silently yields fewer blob bodies. Those missing SHAs then resolve to `bodies.get(b.sha) is None` (skipped) or empty `data={}`, so affected sidecars are dropped or marked unverified — producing a spuriously LOW verified_ratio that is indistinguishable from a genuinely-clean run. Because verified_ratio is the deliverable the manifest feeds into the epic's noise-floor decision, a silent partial read corrupts that input undetectably.
advisory.suggested_fix: After the read loop: `writer.join(); rc = proc.wait();` then `if rc != 0 or len(contents) != len(set(shas)): raise RuntimeError(...)`.

evidence: corpus.py:117-120 `parts = header.split()` then `size = int(parts[2])` with no try/except

advisory.finding: In _batch_cat, `size = int(parts[2])` is executed whenever the header splits into exactly 3 tokens; a malformed but 3-token header (non-numeric third field) raises an uncaught ValueError that aborts the entire corpus build rather than skipping the bad record.

blocking.checklist_item: - [ ] Distinguish reconstruction failure (e.g. no recoverable CREATE, empty reconstructed material) from a genuine fingerprint mismatch, recording a distinct status instead of folding both into `unverified`.
evidence: src/rebar/llm/evals/plan_replay/corpus.py:161-164: `creates = ticket_events.get("CREATE", [])` / `create_data = creates[0]["data"] if creates else {}` / `description = create_data.get("description", "")`
`"verified": generation is not None` (corpus.py:259) — a fingerprint miss is the ONLY signal, whether from a real edit or an empty/incomplete reconstruction
material_basis hashes description+file_impact+children (material_diff.py:133-142); an empty reconstruction hashes to a value that matches no stored fingerprint
ABSENCE: no row field records 'reconstruction had no CREATE' or 'reconstruction incomplete' — unverified is emitted identically in the clean-fail and the never-reconstructed worlds
blocking.finding: The verification oracle cannot distinguish a genuinely-changed (post-review edited) ticket from a reconstruction failure: a ticket with no recoverable CREATE event yields description='' / ticket_type='' (creates[0]['data'] if creates else {}), which silently produces a mismatching fingerprint and is marked `unverified` — the same verdict a truly stale material would get. There is no separate 'reconstruction incomplete / no CREATE found' signal, so the headline verified_ratio (13.4% in the committed manifest) mixes true-unverifiable rows with rows the builder simply failed to reconstruct.
scenarios: A REVIEW_RESULT blob is recovered from git history but the ticket's CREATE blob was compacted/unreachable → row silently counts as unverified rather than 'unreconstructable'
Interpreting verified_ratio 13.4% as 'material changed after review' when much of the gap may be reconstruction gaps

ABSENCE: no counter of dropped/unreadable blobs is surfaced in the manifest, so a run against a partially-fetched or corrupt tracker looks identical to a complete one
dropped.finding: Blob recovery failures and malformed event JSON are swallowed silently, making a partial git-object walk indistinguishable from a clean one. In `_load_ticket_events` a blob whose body could not be read (`bodies.get(b.sha) is None`) is `continue`d and a JSON/attribute error yields `data = {}`; combined with `_batch_cat` skipping any `git cat-file` header that is not 3 parts (a 'missing' object) without recording it, a ticket whose CREATE/EDIT blobs were unreadable is silently reconstructed from partial data and marked unverified with no diagnostic.
scenarios: Running against a shallow clone or a tracker missing some objects → the walk quietly reconstructs from whatever it could read
